To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

space–momentum fluctuations are an important source of correlations in heavy-ion collisions, and that the magnitude and shape of these correlations can be related to the spatial fluctuations in the initial state.

the spatial lumpiness in the initial conditions of a heavy-ion collision can lead to a momentum–space correlation between particles with the same rapidity and that the momentum–space correlation is stronger for particles of higher transverse momentum.

the space–momentum correlation in heavy-ion collisions is a consequence of a collective expansion from lumpy initial conditions, and that these correlations have implications for the initial state and for the collective expansion of the system.

the implications of space–momenta correlations and the role of the initial state geometry on observables in heavy-ion collisions.
